# Chart values

Generated from `charts/spawnery/values.schema.json` -- the schema Helm validates every install and `--set` against -- with defaults read from `charts/spawnery/values.yaml`, the chart's own shipped copy.

Helm validates values.yaml and every --set against this before rendering. It exists because without it a wrong value was rejected by the operator&#x27;s flag parser instead: the container exited at startup with <code>invalid value &quot;30&quot; for flag -startup-deadline</code>, which reaches a cluster as CrashLoopBackOff and names neither the value nor the key. What is validated here is what has actually gone wrong, plus types; the pass-through values (resources, nodeSelector, tolerations, affinity, additionalLabels) are deliberately left open, because a schema that is wrong about them fails an install that would have worked.

Required at the top level: `image`, `operator`.

A blank Description is not a gap: the schema describes only what needs it, and leaves a key bare when its name and type already say what it is.

With both empty the templates render an image reference ending in a colon, and helm&#x27;s own error is a YAML parse failure pointing at deployment.yaml rather than at the value that is missing.</td></tr>

A bare hex string is the shape somebody reaches for first and it is not what a container reference takes. The value checked in at any tag describes the release before it and structurally cannot describe its own: hack/publish.sh takes it from <code>skopeo copy --digestfile</code>, which exists only once the tag is published, so the commit writing it back is necessarily behind the tag it names. Measured on the RKE2 rollout, where a HelmRelease installing the chart at v0.1.0 ran the tag rather than a digest. A deployment that wants an immutable reference pins it where the deployment is described, not here.</td></tr>
